title: Ang 360: the invasion
hookLine: Guru Nanak's hymn on Babur's invasion
tomorrow: what has to die before something can grow?

cards: Something wrong happens right in front of a room, at school, at work, in a group chat, and the room does the usual thing: it changes the subject. Nobody wants to be the one who says it out loud.

On ang 360, Guru Nanak is the one who says it. Tradition links this hymn to Babur's invasion of Punjab. And he speaks straight to God, in paraphrase: so much beating, people cried out; did You feel no pain?
A gentle note for parents: today's hymn is about violence and grief, told without details.

teach.b: The hymn doesn't use polite words. In paraphrase: the Creator sent the Mughal like death's messenger; there was so much slaughter that people screamed.
Then the hard question, aimed upward: did You feel no pain? He goes further.
In paraphrase: if one strong man strikes another, no one is troubled; but when a lion falls on a herd, the herd's master must answer for it.

teach.h: NAME WHAT HAPPENED AND WHO IT HURT.
teach.b: Notice what he does. He doesn't pretend it's fine. He doesn't turn it into a quick lesson about patience.

He names who did it and what it cost, and he takes the complaint right to the top. A hymn can argue with God out loud and still be a hymn. This one sits in the scripture Sikhs bow to, complaint and all.
That's what this page gives an ordinary week. When something is wrong, the first honest thing isn't to make it sound smaller. It's to name it: what happened, who was hurt, and that it mattered.

how: Guru Nanak's hymns on the invasion, which Sikhs call Babarvani, are read in order in Raag Asa and sung as kirtan; Sikhs remember them as the Guru speaking up for people who suffered.

s: Guru Nanak's hymn treats the invasion calmly, as something to accept quietly
he asks God directly: so much beating, people cried out; did You feel no pain?
it says the Creator sent the Mughal like death's messenger.
a hymn that complains to God couldn't be in scripture
this one is in the Guru Granth Sahib, sung as a hymn, complaint and all.

games.q: in your group chat, one friend keeps getting mocked as a 'joke'. everyone sends laughing emojis. what fits ang 360?
o: say plainly that it isn't funny and it's hurting her.
add a laughing emoji so things don't get awkward.
leave the chat quietly and say nothing.
games.why: Guru Nanak didn't change the subject. he named what happened and who it hurt, and took it all the way up.

practice: Read ang 360 if you can, slowly, aloud or in a whisper. Then say one quiet sentence out loud about something wrong you've seen lately: what happened, and who it hurt. No fixing it yet.
Let the rest of the sit be the stillness after a true sentence.
